clue.text: Improvises as daughter inside bails out

indicators.note: the daughter's letter goes inside the rearranged letters, so 'inside' marks the container
'out' as in 'out of order', telling us the letters of bails are jumbled

explanation.surface: An improviser bails out a daughter, perhaps from a sinking boat or a court cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns BAILS into ALIBS, and 'inside' puts D in it to make A-D-LIBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural verb synonym: someone who ad-libs is speaking off the cuff, making it up on the spot.

clue.text: Delicious food in the morning? Bishop more cheerful, we hear

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks a morning time
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: 'we hear' says the pieces are to be spoken and the result is a word that sounds like them

parts.note: rosier means more optimistic or cheerful

explanation.surface: A tasty breakfast puts the bishop in a sunnier mood.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, ROSIER is said like ROSIA, so 'we hear' gives the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the food of the gods, so by extension any exquisitely tasty dish.

clue.text: Satirise a politician taken in by simple-minded person

indicators.note: the politician and 'a' are held inside the word for the fool, so this signals containment

parts.note: a loon is a silly or foolish person
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A satirist mocks a politician who has been duped by a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to ridicule someone publicly through mockery or parody.

clue.text: Head removed from fish covered in cheese in restaurant

indicators.note: the trimmed fish sits wrapped inside the cheese, so this marks containment

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the fish loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: the wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish

explanation.surface: A cook beheads a fish and smothers it in cheese at a bistro.
explanation.walkthrough: The wrasse is a sea fish; 'covered in' puts its headless form inside the soft French cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a French-style eatery, usually informal and serving simple meals.

clue.text: What's needed to log in American before touring Vietnam?

parts.note: US, United States

indicators.note: the word for before goes all round the short name for Vietnam, as a tourist goes round a country

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
Nam is the informal short form of Vietnam

explanation.surface: An American traveller checks what paperwork is needed before touring Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: the identifier you type together with a password to sign in to an account.

clue.text: Radical comes to fancy party member

indicators.note: fancy as a verb is to imagine, or as an adjective elaborate; either way the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A firebrand finally takes a liking to joining a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges all fourteen letters of RADICAL COMES TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of a political party of the centre-left, such as Britain's former SDP.

clue.text: Newly-created earl, leader of men in field

indicators.note: the letters of earl are made anew, a fresh arrangement
the leader is the first letter of men

explanation.surface: A freshly ennobled earl leads his men into a field of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly-created' turns EARL into REAL; M comes from 'leader of men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sphere or domain of activity or knowledge, as in 'the field of physics'.

clue.text: Word of opposite meaning — not many for changing

indicators.note: the letters of 'not many' are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Few people bother to swap a word for its opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NOT MANY gives the answer; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a word meaning the opposite of another, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: What could be nicer? Hotel upgrade

indicators.note: asks what the letters of nicer could become when rearranged

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A happy guest has been moved to a better hotel room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could be' turns NICER into ENRIC, then H is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to improve the quality or value of something.

clue.text: Small cap designed to meet the needs of duke crossing battle site

parts.note: a tam is a Scottish woollen cap, a tam-o'-shanter

parts.words: designed to meet the needs of
parts.note: as in 'made for', something designed for a purpose
a bridge is a crossing over a river

explanation.surface: A milliner makes a small cap to suit a duke's needs.
explanation.walkthrough: STAMFORD BRIDGE, near York, is where Harold II defeated the Norwegian invaders in 1066, just before Hastings.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the site of a famous English battle of 1066, now better known as Chelsea's football ground.

clue.text: Pompous crowing involving doctor in charge

indicators.note: the word for crowing takes in the doctor, wrapping round it

parts.note: crowing, as a noun, is boastful talk: a boast
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

explanation.surface: A self-important doctor boasts about being the one in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: high-flown and inflated in language, showy and self-important.

clue.text: Player's agent ignoring fine

indicators.note: the word for agent passes over the letter for fine, leaving it out

parts.note: a factor is an agent who does business for another
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A performer's agent ignores a fine imposed on him.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a performer on stage or screen who plays a part.

clue.text: Type of furry creature –- work with very large number

parts.note: OP, short for opus, a work
OS, outsize, a clothing size
a sum is a number reached by adding

explanation.surface: Someone works out how many furry animals there are, a very large number.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an American marsupial with a furry coat and a grasping tail.

clue.text: Annual publication bound by local man, a craftsman

indicators.note: the answer is tied up inside these words, held between their letters

explanation.surface: A yearbook is bound by a local man who is a skilled bookbinder.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a yearly book of calendar data, tides and facts, like Old Moore's or Wisden.

clue.text: Victor leaking wife's secret

indicators.note: the victor's word lets the wife's letter escape, losing it

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A champion lets slip his wife's confidences.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: private and hidden from others, as in one's private thoughts.

clue.text: Former sweetheart, model, dancing round apartment, briefly

indicators.note: the rearranged model goes round the short flat, enclosing it
the letters of model dance about into a new order
the word for apartment is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

explanation.surface: An ex-lover, a model, dances around a small flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges the model's letters to OLDME, which splits to go 'round' the shortened apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone you were once in love with, a past romantic partner.

clue.text: Comes down on head creating scene

parts.note: a plane comes down, or lands
a head or headland is a cape

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles onto their head, making quite a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a view of countryside, or a painting of a rural view.

clue.text: Rat in waste, rolling about

parts.note: a desert is a waste or wilderness

indicators.note: the word for about rolls over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A rat rolls about in a waste dump.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a rat is a traitor or turncoat who abandons their side.

clue.text: A theologian facing ruin, then Greek character backed supplement

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity
end as in 'meet one's end', ruin

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes backwards

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A theologian faced with ruin backs a Greek character for support.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an extra section added at the end of a book or document.

clue.text: Fall away, so give up

definitions.meaning: to fall away from a group or race
to quit a course or society, leaving it

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing and abandons the attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to withdraw from something, and also to fall or drop off physically.

clue.text: Husband sitting in pleasant recess

indicators.note: the husband's letter sits inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A husband relaxes in a pleasant alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shallow hollow set into a wall, for a statue or ornament.

clue.text: Talk about run out round island in ceremonial carriage

indicators.note: the word for talk goes about the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: chat is talk

indicators.note: the run and out letters go round the island's letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O can mean out, as zero or nothing

explanation.surface: Gossip about a cricket run-out on an island, in a state coach.
explanation.walkthrough: R and O round I give RIO, and CHAT goes about that.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used in ancient races, processions and triumphs.

clue.text: Second look at cloth sample

parts.note: to watch is to look at

explanation.surface: A shopper takes a second look at a fabric sample.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small piece of fabric shown as an example of the material.

clue.text: Western flea, unusually large thing?

parts.note: a flea is something that hops: a hopper

explanation.surface: A cowboy tells of an enormous flea.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something unusually big, and also a whacking great lie.

clue.text: Schoolchild's young dog left lying under one

indicators.note: in a down clue the left letter sits under the one, coming after it

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A child's puppy has been left lying under someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a student at school, someone taught by a teacher.

clue.text: Conspirator died close to huge waterfall

parts.note: Casca was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar

indicators.note: the close, or end, of huge gives its last letter

explanation.surface: A plotter dies near an enormous waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small waterfall, or a series of them falling over steep rocks.

clue.text: Band in bad taste originally, upon reflection

indicators.note: as in a mirror, the letters are reflected, read backwards

parts.note: poor means bad

indicators.note: originally gives the first letter of taste

explanation.surface: Looking back, a pop group's act was in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: POOR plus T is POORT, which 'upon reflection' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a group of soldiers or people, as in a troop of scouts.

clue.text: Simon, perhaps, having tot with painter right away

parts.note: a tot is a small drink, a dram

indicators.note: right goes away from the painter's word, being taken out

parts.note: a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: Simon has a drink with an artist and leaves at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Neil Simon was an American playwright; ARTIST without R is ATIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the American Neil Simon wrote plays such as The Odd Couple.

clue.text: Ritz, say, providing more comfortable time for male

indicators.note: time stands in for male, taking its place

parts.note: homelier means more cosy and comfortable

explanation.surface: The Ritz offers more comfortable times for gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: César Ritz was the Swiss founder of the Ritz hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: César Ritz ran luxury hotels, as Paris's Ritz still shows.

clue.text: Member of the clergy in park by hill

parts.note: rec, a recreation ground, is a public park
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A churchman strolls in a park near a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a parish priest in the Church of England, in charge of a parish.
